title: Sole Proprietorship, Partnership and Hindu Undivided Family
summary: A business owned, financed, managed and controlled by one person, who takes all the profit and bears all the risk. Examples: a grocery shop, a beauty parlour, a small travel agency. Characteristics: ease of formation (few legal formalities, no registration needed); single ownership (one man's capital); one-man control; unlimited liability — if business assets fall short, the owner's personal property is used to pay creditors; undivided risk; secrecy; no separate legal entity (owner and business are the same); lack of continuity — death or illness can end it.

Advantages: easy to form and close; quick decisions; direct motivation (all profit is the owner's); flexibility; secrecy; personal contact with customers and employees; generates self-employment. Limitations: limited capital (one man's savings and borrowings); limited managerial ability; unlimited liability discourages expansion; uncertain life; not suitable for large-scale business.

Unlimited liability worked out: if business assets are ₹5 lakh, liabilities ₹10 lakh and personal property ₹6 lakh, creditors get the full ₹10 lakh — ₹5 lakh from the business and ₹5 lakh from personal property.

The relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all (Indian Partnership Act, 1932). Members are partners and together a firm. Characteristics: at least two persons (maximum 50 under the Companies Rules; the NIOS text gives 20, 10 for banking); agreement — oral or written (the written one is the partnership deed); lawful business; sharing of profits and losses as agreed (equally if there is no deed); unlimited and joint liability; mutual agency — every partner is both an agent and a principal; utmost good faith; restriction on transfer of interest without consent of all; no separate legal entity; registration is optional; uncertain life — death, insolvency or retirement of a partner can dissolve it. Two people merely sharing the rent of a jointly owned godown are co-owners, not partners, because they carry on no business.

Contents of a partnership deed: name and address of the firm and partners; nature of business; capital contributed by each; profit-sharing ratio; interest on capital and drawings; salaries or commission to partners; rules for admission, retirement and death; method of settling disputes. Advantages: easy formation; more capital and combined skills; balanced decisions; sharing of risk; flexibility; protection of minority interests. Limitations: unlimited liability; uncertain life; limited capital; possible conflict among partners; non-transferability of interest.

Set up under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008. An LLP is a body corporate with a separate legal identity from its partners and perpetual succession; the liability of partners is limited to their agreed contribution; it needs at least two partners (no maximum) and at least two designated partners, one of them resident in India; the rights and duties of partners are governed by the LLP agreement. It combines the flexibility of a partnership with the limited liability of a company.
## Joint Hindu Family (Hindu Undivided Family) business

A business owned by the members of a Joint Hindu Family, governed by Hindu law and the law of succession — found only in India. Members are coparceners (traditionally male members; three successive generations; daughters are coparceners since 2005); membership is by birth (a minor can be a member), not by agreement. Features: management by the Karta (the eldest member), who has unlimited liability, while other coparceners' liability is limited to their share in the HUF property; no maximum number of members; continuity — it is unaffected by the death of a coparcener or even the Karta (the next senior male becomes Karta); registration not needed. Merits: assured economic security, quick decisions by the Karta, continuity, family pride and loyalty, limited liability of members. Limitations: limited capital and managerial skill, unlimited liability of Karta, scope for conflict, dominance of the Karta.

objective: Give one-word answers: (a) Can minors be members of a Hindu Undivided Family business? (b) How many successive generations can be members of an HUF business?

(a) Yes — membership is by birth.
(b) Three.
Fill in the blanks: (a) An LLP has a ________ legal identity from its partners. (b) A partnership requires a minimum of ________ persons.
Ajeet started a travel agency in Shimla in 2020 with his own money and effort, and runs it himself. Identify the form of business organisation. Who bears its risk?

(a) Sole proprietorship.
(b) Ajeet alone bears the entire risk (and gets all the profit).
Write True (T) or False (F): (a) The liability of a sole proprietor is limited. (b) The principle of one person one vote applies to sole proprietorship.

(a) False — it is unlimited.
(b) False — it applies to cooperative societies.

Mr. Vikas winds up his sole proprietorship with assets of ₹5 lakh and liabilities of ₹8 lakh. He has personal property of ₹8 lakh. (a) How much will creditors get? (b) From where will the balance come?

(a) ₹8 lakh — the full amount.
(b) ₹5 lakh from business assets and the balance ₹3 lakh from his personal property, because his liability is unlimited.
The business assets of an organisation are worth ₹90,000 but its unpaid debts are ₹1,20,000. In a sole proprietorship, what can the creditors do?

(a) Take the ₹90,000 of business assets.
(b) Recover the balance ₹30,000 from the proprietor's personal property, because his liability is unlimited.
vsa: 'This form of organisation is found only in India.' Identify it and state two of its features.

Joint Hindu Family (HUF) business.
(1) Membership by birth — a child becomes a member on birth; no agreement is needed.
(2) The Karta (eldest member) manages it and has unlimited liability, while other members' liability is limited to their share.
State any two contents of a partnership deed.

Any two: name and address of the firm and partners; nature of business; capital of each partner; profit-sharing ratio; interest on capital and drawings; salaries to partners; rules for admission, retirement and settlement of disputes.
State two features of a Limited Liability Partnership.

(1) It is a body corporate with a separate legal identity from its partners, and perpetual succession.
(2) The liability of each partner is limited to his agreed contribution.
(Also: at least two partners and two designated partners; governed by the LLP agreement.)

Satish lost his job and wants to start a business with little money and few legal formalities. Suggest a form of organisation. OR Rohan and Sachin bought a godown with equal money and share its rent equally. Are they partners?

Satish: sole proprietorship — easy to start with little capital and almost no legal formalities.
Rohan and Sachin are not partners: they are only co-owners sharing income from property; there is no business carried on by them.
What is a partnership? Explain in your own words.

A partnership is an agreement between two or more persons to carry on a lawful business together and share its profits and losses. Each partner contributes capital or skill, takes part in management and has unlimited liability; the partners together are called a firm.
Pankaj and four friends start a business by an agreement about profit sharing, duties and rights. Identify the form and state two characteristics.

Partnership.
(1) Agreement — the relationship arises from an oral or written agreement (deed).
(2) Unlimited liability and mutual agency — every partner is personally liable and can act for the firm.
sa: State any three limitations of Joint Hindu Family business.

(1) Limited capital — only family property and borrowings.
(2) Limited managerial ability — the Karta may not have all the skills.
(3) Unlimited liability of the Karta discourages risk-taking and expansion.
(4) Scope for conflict among members and dominance of the Karta. (Any three.)
State any three limitations of a partnership firm.

(1) Unlimited liability — partners' personal property can be taken for firm's debts.
(2) Uncertain life — death, insolvency or retirement of a partner may end it.
(3) Limited capital — partners are few in number.
(4) Possible conflict and lack of harmony; interest cannot be transferred without consent. (Any three.)
Define sole proprietorship. Write any four features.

A business owned, managed and controlled by one person who takes all the profit and bears all the risk.
Features: (1) single ownership; (2) one-man control; (3) unlimited liability; (4) ease of formation; also secrecy, undivided risk, no separate legal entity, lack of continuity.
'A sole proprietorship is the best form of organisation if the owner can handle everything.' Explain any five advantages of sole proprietorship.

(1) Easy to form and close — few legal formalities.
(2) Quick decisions — the owner need not consult anyone.
(3) Direct motivation — all the profit goes to the owner, so he works hard.
(4) Secrecy — business information stays with the owner.
(5) Personal contact with customers and employees, and flexibility to change with the market.
Describe briefly any four characteristics of sole proprietorship.

(1) Single ownership — one person owns and finances it.
(2) One-man control — he takes all decisions.
(3) Unlimited liability — personal property is liable for business debts.
(4) No separate legal entity and lack of continuity — business and owner are the same, and death or illness may end it.
la: Gopal (Karta) and his family run an HUF business that took a ₹20 lakh loan. They repaid only ₹10 lakh by selling ancestral property. The court held that the other members were liable only to the extent of their share, but Gopal had to pay the balance from his personal property. (a) Give reasons for the court's decision. (b) State three other features of HUF business.

(a) In an HUF the Karta has unlimited liability — his personal assets can be used to pay business debts. Other coparceners have limited liability up to their share in the HUF property. As the HUF property was already sold, only the Karta's personal property was left to repay the balance.
(b) (1) Membership by birth — no agreement is needed. (2) Management by the Karta. (3) Continuity — unaffected by the death of a member. (4) No maximum number of members; governed by Hindu law.

or: Business assets are ₹2,00,000 but unpaid debts are ₹3,00,000. What can the creditors do if (a) it is a sole proprietorship (b) it is a partnership of A and B sharing profits equally?

(a) Sole proprietorship: creditors take the ₹2,00,000 of business assets and recover the balance ₹1,00,000 from the proprietor's personal property, because his liability is unlimited.
(b) Partnership: creditors take the ₹2,00,000 and recover the balance ₹1,00,000 from the personal property of A and B, who are jointly and severally liable — the creditors may recover it from either or both (each bears ₹50,000 between themselves).

la: Ramita and two friends open 'Apna Bhoj' with ₹80,000 each, sharing profits equally, each liable for the acts of the others. (a) Identify the form of organisation. (b) Explain any four of its characteristics.

(a) Partnership.
(b) (1) Two or more persons — here three friends.
(2) Agreement — they agreed on capital and profit sharing.
(3) Sharing of profits — equally, as agreed.
(4) Mutual agency — each partner is an agent of the others and liable for their acts.
(5) Unlimited liability — their personal property can be used for the firm's debts.
Sanjay and Mohan want to run a business together and share profits and losses in the ratio of their capital. Identify the form and explain five features.

Partnership.
(1) At least two persons and an agreement (preferably a written deed).
(2) Lawful business carried on for profit.
(3) Sharing of profits and losses in the agreed ratio (here the capital ratio).
(4) Unlimited liability of partners.
(5) Mutual agency, utmost good faith and restriction on transfer of interest.
'This business exists under Hindu law and is governed by the law of succession.' Identify it and state its features.

Joint Hindu Family (HUF) business.
(1) Membership by birth — coparceners of three generations.
(2) Management by the Karta, the eldest member.
(3) Liability — unlimited for the Karta, limited to their share for other members.
(4) Continuity — unaffected by the death of any member, including the Karta.
(5) No registration needed; no maximum number of members.
What is partnership? Explain any four advantages of the partnership form of business.

Partnership is the relation between persons who agree to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
(1) Easy formation — only an agreement is needed.
(2) More capital and combined skills of several partners.
(3) Balanced decisions after discussion.
(4) Sharing of risk among partners.
(5) Flexibility and close supervision.
